title: Podgora Cost Guide 2027: Daily Budgets and Prices
metaDescription: What a trip to Podgora costs in 2027: rooms, meals, drinks, buses, transfers and daily budgets for the Makarska Riviera town, all in euros.
content:
## How Much Does a Trip to Podgora Cost?

Podgora is a small town on the Makarska Riviera, about 10 km south of Makarska. It is cheaper than Makarska itself and clearly cheaper than Split, Hvar or Dubrovnik, although prices climb sharply from July to mid-August. Croatia uses the euro, so all figures below are in €.

### Daily Budget by Travel Style

| Style | Per person per day (peak season) | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | €60–90 | Shared apartment room, supermarket meals, one restaurant dinner, beach days |
| Mid-range | €110–160 | Private apartment or 3–4 star hotel, restaurant lunch or dinner, a drink or two |
| Comfortable | €200+ | Beachfront resort, half board or daily restaurant meals, boat trip |

Couples sharing an apartment spread the room cost, so the per-person figure falls noticeably. In June and September, cut the accommodation portion by 25–40%.

## Accommodation Prices in Podgora

### Apartments and Private Rooms

Private apartments dominate. Off-peak double rooms and studios start around €35–60 per night, and well-rated apartments with a balcony typically run €65–130. In July and August, expect €90–150 for a decent apartment near the sea, and more for new design apartments or villas. Villas with pools can exceed €250 per night.

Many hosts require a minimum stay of 5–7 nights in July and August. Stays shorter than that often carry a surcharge or are refused. Tourist tax is added on top, usually a few euros per person per night in summer.

### Hotels and Resorts

- **Medora Auri Family Beach Resort**: the main beachfront hotel, rated around 4.2 out of 5 by more than 690 reviewers. Rooms typically cost €100–150 per night, with half board packages available.
- **Hotel Liberan**: a smaller hotel with a pool, usually €70–95 per night in season.
- **Medora Orbis Camping & Glamping**: rated about 4.5 out of 5, with glamping units costing noticeably more than a standard pitch.

Beach hotels in nearby Tučepi, such as TUI Blue Adriatic Beach, tend to cost more, from roughly €180–200 per night in shoulder season for adults-only all-inclusive.

Tripadvisor's average listed hotel price for Podgora sits around €130–140 per night, which is skewed upward by resorts. Apartments are the better value.

### When Prices Drop

June and September offer sea temperatures of 22–25°C with room rates well below August levels. May and October are cheaper still, but beach clubs and some restaurants reduce hours or close. This is the best value period for the town.

## Food and Drink Prices

### Restaurants

Podgora has a waterfront strip of konobas and seafood restaurants. Well-known names include Roko Restaurant (rated about 4.5 from 640+ reviews), Vruja, More, Ahipara and Konoba Borak. Typical 2027 prices:

- Grilled fish (priced per kg): €60–90 per kg, usually one fish per two people costs €35–55
- Meat or pasta main: €12–22
- Seafood risotto or black risotto: €14–20
- Pizza: €9–13 (Portobello Bar Pizzeria is the highly rated budget pick)
- Starter or salad: €6–12
- Dinner for two with wine at mid-range seafood restaurant: €60–100

A mid-range meal runs roughly €15–25 per person, with dinners at the waterfront on the higher side.

### Drinks and Coffee

- Espresso or macchiato: €1.80–2.50
- Local draft beer (0.3–0.5 l): €3–4.50
- Glass of house wine: €3.50–5
- Cocktail at a beach bar: €9–13
- Water (0.5 l) in a café: €2.50–3.50

### Supermarkets and Bakeries

Supermarkets such as Konzum and Studenac serve the town. A burek or a sandwich from a bakery costs €2–4, which makes a quick lunch cheap. A week of self-catering breakfast and lunch for two costs roughly €80–120.

## Getting There and Getting Around

### From Split Airport and Split

Podgora is about 71–94 km from Split depending on the route and stop, and the trip takes around 1h 15m by road.

- **Bus from Split**: about €11–14 one way with Promet Makarska and other operators. Journey is 1h 20m to 1h 55m.
- **Private transfer**: from about €103–120 per vehicle, up to 3–4 passengers. This works out cheaper per person than a bus for groups of four.
- **Rental car**: €35–80 per day in summer, plus fuel and about €12–16 in tolls and fuel combined for a one-way run from Split to the Riviera.
- **Taxi from Makarska**: about €30–40 for the 10 km ride.

### Local Buses

The bus to Makarska takes 10–15 minutes and costs roughly €1–4. It runs on a limited schedule, so check timetables at the stop. Most visitors walk the coastal path within Podgora, and no car is needed for the town itself.

### Parking

Most apartments include free parking. Public parking in the centre is paid in summer, typically €1–2 per hour.

## Activities and Extras

- Beach: free. Pebble beaches along the promenade are public. Sunbed and umbrella set costs €10–20 per day at hotel and beach-club areas.
- Boat taxi or excursion to Brač, Hvar or Makarska coves: €30–60 per person for half-day trips.
- Biokovo Nature Park visit (Skywalk and entrance): entrance fees are around €10–15 per person, plus a car or tour to get there.
- Rafting on the Cetina and Omiš day trips: roughly €40–70 per person including transport.
- Day trip to Hvar by ferry from Makarska or Split: €14–22 one way depending on route.

## Local Money-Saving Tips

- Book apartments outside July and August. The saving is often 30–40% for the same unit.
- Eat the main meal at lunch. Many restaurants offer a daily menu or smaller portions at lower prices than at dinner.
- Check whether apartments include beach towels, parking and air conditioning. Air conditioning is sometimes charged extra per day.
- Avoid ordering fish without asking the per-kilogram price. Fish is sold by weight, and the bill can surprise visitors.
- Do not pay for a Split private transfer if you are travelling alone. The €11–14 bus is far better value, and the extra €90+ buys little more than convenience.
- Use Makarska for larger grocery shops, since supermarket prices are slightly lower and the selection wider.
- Pay in cash for small purchases. Cards are accepted in most restaurants, but a few small beach kiosks and rooms are cash only.

## Is Podgora Cheaper Than Makarska?

Yes, modestly. Accommodation and dining run roughly 10–20% below Makarska's seafront. The trade-off is fewer nightlife options and a quieter promenade. Podgora suits families and couples. Visitors who want clubs and a large pedestrian centre pay more in Makarska.

## Sample 7-Day Budget for Two (July)

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Apartment, 7 nights at €100 | €700 |
| Meals (4 restaurant dinners at €50, groceries €100, coffees and drinks €70) | €370 |
| Bus transfers or shared transfer from Split | €30–220 |
| One boat excursion for two | €90 |
| Sunbeds, parking, extras | €80 |
| **Total** | **€1,270–1,460** |

That works out to about €90–105 per person per day, with room to cut by travelling in June or September.

faq.question: How much money do I need per day in Podgora?
faq.answer: A budget traveller needs about €60–90 per day in peak season, mid-range visitors €110–160, and resort guests €200 or more. Costs drop 25–40% in June and September.

faq.question: Is Podgora expensive compared with other Croatian destinations?
faq.answer: No. Podgora is cheaper than Makarska, Split, Hvar and Dubrovnik, especially for apartments and restaurant meals. Prices still rise sharply in July and August.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Podgora?
faq.answer: A pizza or pasta costs about €9–15, and a seafood or meat main at a waterfront restaurant €14–25. Dinner for two with wine at a mid-range seafood place runs about €60–100.

faq.question: How do I get from Split to Podgora and what does it cost?
faq.answer: The bus takes about 1h 20m and costs roughly €11–14 one way. A private transfer takes about 1h 15m and starts around €103–120 per vehicle.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Podgora?
faq.answer: May, late September and October have the lowest accommodation prices, though some seasonal venues close. June and September balance warm sea temperatures with prices 25–40% below August.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Podgora?
faq.answer: No. The town is walkable, and buses reach Makarska in about 10–15 minutes for €1–4. A car only helps for visits to Biokovo, Cetina or remote coves.

faq.question: Does Podgora use euros and are cards accepted?
faq.answer: Yes, Croatia uses the euro. Restaurants, hotels and supermarkets accept cards, but carry some cash for small kiosks, private rooms and parking machines.

quickAnswer: Podgora costs about €60–90 per person per day on a budget, €110–160 at mid-range and €200+ in peak summer at beachfront resorts. Apartments start near €40–60 per night off-peak. A restaurant main costs €12–25, a beer €3–4.50, and the bus to Makarska about €1–4.
